criteria.ambient_scope: Dispatch opens one request scope per handler run that packages the shared budget, an abort signal, and a place to file escalations, and SQL plus fetch adapters resolve it implicitly, so disconnects and shutdown expire each outstanding operation separately with its own unknown-write outcome and escalation note; explicitly passed caller bounds still resolve to the smaller of bound and remainder.
criteria.outer_race: Dispatch constrains only the handler as a unit against the request budget, and when that budget lapses it returns a single bounded reply with one request-wide escalation while the handler drains out of sight, leaving enclosed operations to finish without per-operation unknown-write outcomes or escalation notes.

propagation.instructions: Which mechanism should move disconnect and shutdown expiry from the dispatcher down into live operations?

criteria.new_failure: Define a purpose-built catalogue failure like sql::operation_unknown and register it in the emits of all budgeted SQL calls, which writes boundary expiry into the checked error union plainly but demands catalogue regeneration, checker and emitter changes, and migration of the existing examples owned elsewhere.
criteria.reuse_query_failed: Signal SQL boundary expiry via the extant sql::query_failed failure together with a documented code string (the operation slot holds the call name, the code slot holds budget), which needs zero catalogue, checker, or emitter work; Can handlers discriminate on the code while the adapter renders the shared unknown-write marker as this domain value.

sql_failure.instructions: Which failure should a budgeted SQL call return once its visible boundary answers at the bound with the native query still owned?

criteria.status_400: Serve a body read that outruns its stall bound with the current fixed 400 for body read failures, preserving the rejected-status union exactly and equating stalls with malformed bodies.
criteria.status_408: Serve a body read that outruns its stall bound with a fixed 408 Request Timeout, widening the rejected-status union to include 408, while malformed bodies stay at 400 and oversize bodies stay at 413.

stall_status.instructions: Which status code should bounded ingress use after a body read exceeds its stall bound?

state: Can compiles to TypeScript adapters executed directly on Bun 1.4.2; nobody outside the project consumes them, so past behavior carries no retention requirement. Direct measurements establish the constraints: Bun.SQL Query.cancel merely flips a per-client flag across the PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite dialects while each backend continues through normal completion, and cancelling ahead of execution produces an await that never settles, so SQL must use the cancel-absent branch in which the visible boundary replies when the operation bound lapses, the native query remains owned until it settles, and the delivered outcome reports honestly unknown under supervisor escalation. The serve-side Request.signal trips soon after peer disconnect yet on its own halts no work, so it counts only as disconnect observation. The already landed E01 stratum supplies one shared budget per request with the effective deadline defined as the minimum of the operation bound and the remaining budget, a frozen unknown-write marker of commit unknown, owned, and supervisor escalation common to SQL, fetch, action, S3, and worker paths, closing behavior that drains first, and leases no timer can revoke. Binding interface rules insist on finite explicit emits, exactly one unknown-write vocabulary, and caller operands restricted to natively verified meanings; the checker and emitter belong to sibling lanes, whereas runtime files, tests, and the catalogue merges for these sections belong to this task. Existing failure values comprise sql::query_failed with operation and code strings, sql::commit_unknown carrying a transaction id for the transaction path, http::timeout carrying timeout_ms, and http::transport_failed carrying a phase string. Present-day ingress consumes request bodies unbounded, responding to read failures with a fixed 400 and to excessive size with a fixed 413.
